judge_input.description:
# Summary of Changes

What this particular change here does, at the very core of it, is to go right ahead and deprecate `falcon.testing.redirected`, and it goes about doing this specifically and deliberately in favor of instead making use of the standard library's very own `contextlib.redirect_stdout`, taken together with its close companion `contextlib.redirect_stderr`, in its place instead.

**Changes:**
- Went ahead and added a deprecation warning directly onto `falcon.testing.redirected`, and this was accomplished specifically by way of making use of the `falcon.util.deprecated` helper that already exists for exactly this sort of purpose
- Went and updated the internal test file (that is to say, the particular one which is named `test_cmd_inspect_app.py`) in such a way that it now goes ahead and makes use of the `contextlib` alternatives instead of whatever it happened to be using before this change
- This whole thing has been scheduled and lined up in such a way that the eventual and final removal of it is going to end up happening at the point once we finally reach the Falcon 5.0 release

**Rationale:**
- The very popular pytest framework already goes ahead, entirely on its own, and captures and then subsequently suppresses the output that happens to come out of the tests that were successful, and, importantly, it does the whole of this automatically and by default without ever having to be asked
- The stdlib all by itself already goes and provides the exact equivalent functionality for this, and it does so by way of offering up both `contextlib.redirect_stdout` and also, alongside it, `contextlib.redirect_stderr`
- It goes on to reduce the ongoing maintenance burden that we have to carry around on our shoulders, and the way that it manages to do this is by going and removing a utility which had, by this particular point in time, ended up becoming genuinely redundant

# Related Issues

Fixes #2569

# Pull Request Checklist

This part right here is really nothing at all more than just a simple and friendly little reminder concerning the mistakes that turn out to be the most common ones that people tend to make. Please do go well out of your way to make absolutely and completely sure that you go carefully through and tick every single last one of the *appropriate* boxes. Reading all the way through our [contribution guide](https://falcon.readthedocs.io/en/stable/community/contributing.html), and doing so at the very least one single time, is the kind of thing that is going to end up saving you a good handful of review cycles somewhere further on down the line!

If it should turn out to be the case that some particular one of the items does not actually end up applying in any real way to your own particular pull request as it stands, then the thing that you ought to do at that point is to go right ahead and **check it anyway**, and the reason for that is because the very act of going and doing exactly that is the thing which makes it plainly, clearly, and unmistakably apparent to each and every one of the people looking that there is genuinely and truly nothing at all which is actually in need of being done at all in that particular spot.

- [x] Applied all of the changes across to both the WSGI code path and the ASGI code path, as well as to each of their respective interfaces (in each and every single one of the places throughout the codebase where doing such a thing turns out to be genuinely applicable and appropriate to carry out).
- [x] Added a whole set of **tests** that go on to properly and thoroughly cover the specific portion of the code which happened to be the part that was changed and touched as a part of this particular piece of work here.
- [x] Performed each and all of the automated tests, along with running the various different code quality checks that are expected, and did the whole of that by way of [running `tox`](https://falcon.readthedocs.io/en/stable/community/contributing.html#pull-requests).
- [x] Prefixed every single one of the code comments with a GitHub nick, placing that together alongside an appropriate prefix that sits right there in front of it at the start of the comment.
- [x] The coding style used throughout the entirety of this change has been kept fully and very carefully consistent with the particular coding style that is used across the whole of the rest of the framework as it stands.
- [x] Updated the **documentation** in such a way and to such a degree that it now properly and accurately covers the code which happened to be changed here as part of the work.
    - [x] Added docstrings for any and absolutely every single one of the new classes, the new functions, or the new modules that happened to be introduced over the course of this change.
    - [x] Updated all of the various docstrings so as to properly reflect any and all of the modifications that ended up being made over to the code which was already existing beforehand.
    - [x] Updated both the WSGI documentation and also the ASGI documentation (in each and every place wherever it happens to be applicable to go and do so).
    - [x] Added references that point over to the new classes, the new functions, or the new modules, going ahead and placing each of them into the relevant RST file which happens to live under the `docs/` directory.
    - [x] Updated each and every last one of the relevant supporting documentation files that are being kept and maintained under the `docs/` directory.
    - [x] A copyright notice has been duly included right up at the very top of any and all of the new modules (making use of either your own personal name, or else instead making use of the name that belongs to your organization).
    - [x] The classes, methods, and functions that were either changed or added all carry the appropriate `versionadded`, `versionchanged`, or `deprecated` [directives](http://www.sphinx-doc.org/en/stable/usage/restructuredtext/directives.html?highlight=versionadded#directive-versionadded).
- [x] The changes (together with any deprecations that might possibly be involved) have [towncrier news fragments](https://falcon.readthedocs.io/en/stable/community/contributing.html#changelog) that have been placed under the `docs/_newsfragments/` directory, each one with a file name that follows the format `{issue_number}.{fragment_type}.rst`. (Go ahead and run `tox -e towncrier`, and then go and inspect `docs/_build/html/changes/` over in the browser in order to make certain for yourself that the whole thing renders correctly.)
- [x] Any LLM output at all, if it should happen that there is indeed any of it whatsoever, has been very carefully reviewed and then also properly tested by an actual human developer. (See also, for more on this: [Use of LLMs ("AI")](https://falcon.readthedocs.io/en/latest/community/contributing.html#use-of-llms-ai).)

In the event that you should happen to find yourself holding onto *any* questions whatsoever, of any kind at all, regarding *any* one of the individual points that have been listed out up above here in this section, then please, by all means, simply go right ahead and **submit and ask** the question that is on your mind! This entire checklist here has been put together and placed here for the express and sole purpose of genuinely trying its best to *help* you along on your way, and it is most certainly and absolutely not here for the purpose of deterring you in any way, in any shape, or in any form whatsoever from going ahead and making your contribution!

+The :func:`falcon.testing.redirected` context manager has been deprecated in

+# NOTE(TudorGR): Deprecated in Falcon 4.3.

+@falcon.util.deprecated(
+    'This context manager is deprecated and will be removed in Falcon 5.0. '
+    'Please use contextlib.redirect_stdout and contextlib.redirect_stderr instead.'

 @contextlib.contextmanager

     stdout: TextIO = sys.stdout, stderr: TextIO = sys.stderr

+        :func:`contextlib.redirect_stderr` instead.

     old_stdout, old_stderr = sys.stdout, sys.stderr
